exposure: psychotherapeutic medication types (antidepressants, anxiolytics/sedatives, anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, stimulants)
demographic and clinical characteristics (e.g., employment status)
outcome: continuation of psychotherapeutic medications during pregnancy
discontinuation of psychotherapeutic medications during pregnancy
cohort: The study included women using psychotherapeutic medications (antidepressants, anxiolytics/sedatives, anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, and stimulants) during pregnancy in the U.S. from 2008 to 2015.
finding: Antidepressants were the most commonly discontinued psychotherapeutic medication during pregnancy, whereas antipsychotics were more likely to be continued, and women who continued medications were less likely to be employed.
